verdict.rationale: Reader offers no documented region or residency selector for its hosted SaaS. It does ship a prebuilt self-hostable image and lets you point its page cache at an S3-compatible bucket you choose, so a self-hosting user controls where fetched data is stored. That is only indirect, partial support for residency choice. Missing for 10: region selection for the hosted r.jina.ai service, documented data-residency or retention policy, guarantees covering all stored data (not just the cache), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Point Reader at an S3-compatible bucket to cache fetched pages and reuse them across requests
A prebuilt image of the open-source branch is published to GitHub Container Registry.
